The Philosophy

Ancestral
Futurism

"The ancestors did not live in the past. They built the future. We are the ceremony they were performing."

Not Nostalgia

The most advanced technology on Earth is the oldest.
It lives in the knowledge of indigenous people.
In the earth. In the mineral. In the ritual.

ReturnTo what has always been true
RitualThe technology of presence
ReceiveThe mineral. The land. The now.
Why Honolulu

Tokyo was genesis.
Honolulu is homecoming.

On Pele's island. July 2026.

The Evening

Arc of the
Ceremony

July 2026 · 5:30 PM — 11:00 PM

The Ceremony Arc

Every Moment
Intentional

5:30 PM

Puka Hou — The Opening

Torchlit arrival. Maile lei. VIVĀRA drops on volcanic stone. Hula kahiko begins before anyone announces it.

6:15 PM

Oli Aloha — The Invocation

One pū blown once. Kumu hula dedicates the evening to the land, the ancestors, the future.

6:35 PM

Ka Hana — The Practice

The Vessel. The origin story told. First drop taken in unison. Sixty seconds of complete silence.

7:00 PM

ʻAha ʻAina — The Sacred Meal

5-course feast by a Native Hawaiian chef. All island-sourced. Provenance spoken before each course.

8:45 PM

Kamaʻilio — The Transmission

One invited Hawaiian voice. Not a panel. A transmission on ancestral intelligence and mineral medicine.

9:30 PM

Pō Nani — The Beautiful Night

After-hours exclusive gallery access. Ten millennia of Pacific art. The museum becomes a temple.

7:00 PM · The Feast

ʻAha ʻAina
The Sacred Meal

Native Hawaiian chef · 5 courses · All island-sourced · No fusion

The Cultural Layer

Mālama Honua

We are not staging a moment on Hawaiian land.
We are being received by it.

Every element of this ceremony lives in service to the culture that holds us. We arrived as guests. We act like it.

Cultural Integration

Four Pillars

01 ʻĀina Aloha

All food and botanicals from Native Hawaiian growers. No exceptions.

02 Pele's Thread

Shilajit from volcanic earth. Told on the island where that story lives.

03 Hōkūleʻa Way

Polynesian star navigation as the event's visual language.

04 Oli & Hula

Not performance. Invocation. Living prayer.

The Give-Back Commitment

A portion of every ticket returns to the Hawaiian people.

This event does not extract — it reciprocates. Revenue from Kōkua track tickets is pre-allocated to Native Hawaiian cultural organizations before the event opens.

We arrived as guests. We act like it.

Cultural Partners
  • Office of Hawaiian Affairs (OHA)
  • Polynesian Voyaging Society — Hōkūleʻa
  • Bishop Museum — Language Preservation
  • ʻAha Pūnana Leo — Hawaiian Language Nests
  • Mālama ʻĀina — Native Land Stewardship

Production Design

The Material
World

Fire & LightVolcanic Installation

Basalt lava-stone fire table. LED amber/teal wash on HoMA's colonnades. Only fire and the sky.

Textiles & ObjectsKapa & Sacred Objects

Kapa-pattern runners. Hand-carved koa cups. Volcanic stone card holders — blessed morning-of. All gifted.

SoundFrom Silence to Song

Arrival: Waimea Falls recordings. Ceremony: one pū blown. Dinner: live steel guitar and ipu heke.

Dress CodeAncestral Futurism

Ancient materials in a future silhouette. Bone, obsidian, amber, star-white. Traditional adornment welcomed.

The Intention

The Future
Was Ancient

On Pele's island, in a museum that holds ten thousand years of Pacific memory, sixty people will take the mineral, hear the chant, and remember what the most advanced civilizations on Earth already knew.

E ola mau — May it live on forever
